1	---
2	layout: default
3	title : "Setoid.Subalgebras.Basic module (The Agda Universal Algebra Library)"
4	date : "2021-07-17"
5	author: "agda-algebras development team"
6	---
7	
8	#### Subalgebras of setoid algebras
9	
10	This is the [Setoid.Subalgebras.Basic][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
11	
12	`𝑨` is a **subalgebra** of `𝑩`, written `𝑨 ≤ 𝑩`, just in case `𝑨` can be
13	*homomorphically embedded* in `𝑩`: there is a homomorphism from `𝑨` to `𝑩` whose
14	underlying map is injective.
15	
16	Note that the notion of subalgebra that we define here is different from the
17	standard textbook definition, which defines a *subuniverse* to be a subset of
18	the carrier of an algebra that is closed under the operations (as we do in the
19	[Setoid.Subalgebras.Subuniverses][] module); a subalgebra is then a subuniverse
20	together with the operations of the larger algebra restricted to it.  Nothing in
21	our definition requires the carrier of a subalgebra of `𝑩` to be a subset of the
22	carrier of `𝑩`.[^1]
23	
24	Our subalgebra relation `_≤_`{.AgdaFunction} is clearly reflexive and transitive,
25	so it is a *preorder*; that is exactly what [Setoid.Subalgebras.Properties][]
26	proves, as `≤-preorder`{.AgdaFunction}, and it is the only order-theoretic fact
27	about `_≤_`{.AgdaFunction} that this subtree establishes.
28	
29	It is not a partial order.  Antisymmetry would require that `𝑨 ≤ 𝑩` and `𝑩 ≤ 𝑨`
30	imply `𝑨 ≈ 𝑩` for some suitable `≈`, and read as "on the nose" equality that
31	plainly fails.  The tempting repair is to read `≈` as isomorphism, but that fails
32	too: `𝑨 ≤ 𝑩` and `𝑩 ≤ 𝑨` supply injective homomorphisms in both directions, and a
33	pair of injections is not an isomorphism.  Neither map need invert the other, and
34	in general no isomorphism need exist at all — the free groups on two and on three
35	generators embed in each other yet are not isomorphic, as their abelianizations
36	`ℤ²` and `ℤ³` already show.  Extracting a bijection from two injections is
37	Cantor–Bernstein, which is unavailable constructively, and the bijection it
38	yields classically need not be a homomorphism.
39	
40	For **finite** algebras the repair does work, and that is the setting much of this
41	library's later work lives in.  Mutual injections between finite carriers force
42	equal cardinality; an injective map between finite sets of equal cardinality is
43	surjective; and an injective, surjective homomorphism is an isomorphism, by
44	`Bijective→≅`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Isomorphisms][].  So on
45	finite algebras `_≤_`{.AgdaFunction} is antisymmetric up to isomorphism, hence a
46	partial order on isomorphism classes.  That chain of reasoning is *not* formalized
47	here; only `Bijective→≅`{.AgdaFunction}, its last step, is.
48	
49	This module defines the subalgebra relation `_≤_`{.AgdaFunction} and the several
50	ways of packaging it: as a record bundling both algebras, as a Σ-type over the
51	smaller algebra with the larger one fixed, and relative to a whole class rather
52	than to a single algebra.  The class-relative form `_≤c_`{.AgdaFunction} is the
53	one the closure operator `S`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Varieties.Closure][] is
54	built from.
55

60	module Setoid.Subalgebras.Basic where
61	
62	open import Agda.Primitive using () renaming ( Set to Type )
63	
64	-- imports from the Agda Standard Library ---------------------------------------------------
65	open import Data.Product          using ( _,_ ; Σ-syntax ) renaming ( _×_ to _∧_ )
66	open import Level                 using ( Level ; _⊔_ )
67	open import Relation.Unary        using ( Pred ; _∈_ )
68	
69	-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library ------------------------------------------
70	open import Overture              using ( proj₁ ; proj₂ ; Signature ; 𝓞 ; 𝓥 )
71	open import Setoid.Algebras       using ( Algebra ; ov )
72	open import Setoid.Functions      using ( IsInjective )
73	open import Setoid.Homomorphisms  using ( hom ; mon ; mon→intohom ; kerquo ; FirstHomTheorem )

75	private variable α ρᵃ β ρᵇ ℓ : Level

77	-->
78	
79	The relation comes in two directions and three packagings.
80	
81	+  `_IsSubalgebraOf_`{.AgdaFunction}, with the infix alias `_≤_`{.AgdaFunction},
82	   is the relation itself: `𝑨 ≤ 𝑩` is the type of pairs `(h , inj)` with
83	   `h : hom 𝑨 𝑩` and `inj` a proof that the underlying map of `h` is injective.
84	+  `_IsSupalgebraOf_`{.AgdaFunction}, aliased `_≥_`{.AgdaFunction}, is the
85	   converse, and is *definitionally* the same type read the other way round:
86	   `𝑨 ≤ 𝑩` and `𝑩 ≥ 𝑨` both unfold to an injective homomorphism from `𝑨` into
87	   `𝑩`.
88	+  `mon→≤`{.AgdaFunction} turns a monomorphism into a proof of the subalgebra
89	   relation.  It is immediate, because `mon→intohom`{.AgdaFunction} of
90	   [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Basic][] already produces exactly this type.
91	+  `SubalgebraOf`{.AgdaRecord} bundles both algebras and the proof into a single
92	   record.  `Subalgebra`{.AgdaFunction} instead fixes the larger algebra and
93	   collects the smaller one with its embedding, so an inhabitant of
94	   `Subalgebra 𝑨` is a pair `(𝑩 , p)` with `p : 𝑩 ≤ 𝑨`.
95

#### Subalgebras of setoid algebras

This is the [Setoid.Subalgebras.Basic][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].

`𝑨` is a **subalgebra** of `𝑩`, written `𝑨 ≤ 𝑩`, just in case `𝑨` can be
*homomorphically embedded* in `𝑩`: there is a homomorphism from `𝑨` to `𝑩` whose
underlying map is injective.

Note that the notion of subalgebra that we define here is different from the
standard textbook definition, which defines a *subuniverse* to be a subset of
the carrier of an algebra that is closed under the operations (as we do in the
[Setoid.Subalgebras.Subuniverses][] module); a subalgebra is then a subuniverse
together with the operations of the larger algebra restricted to it.  Nothing in
our definition requires the carrier of a subalgebra of `𝑩` to be a subset of the
carrier of `𝑩`.[^1]

Our subalgebra relation `_≤_`{.AgdaFunction} is clearly reflexive and transitive,
so it is a *preorder*; that is exactly what [Setoid.Subalgebras.Properties][]
proves, as `≤-preorder`{.AgdaFunction}, and it is the only order-theoretic fact
about `_≤_`{.AgdaFunction} that this subtree establishes.

It is not a partial order.  Antisymmetry would require that `𝑨 ≤ 𝑩` and `𝑩 ≤ 𝑨`
imply `𝑨 ≈ 𝑩` for some suitable `≈`, and read as "on the nose" equality that
plainly fails.  The tempting repair is to read `≈` as isomorphism, but that fails
too: `𝑨 ≤ 𝑩` and `𝑩 ≤ 𝑨` supply injective homomorphisms in both directions, and a
pair of injections is not an isomorphism.  Neither map need invert the other, and
in general no isomorphism need exist at all — the free groups on two and on three
generators embed in each other yet are not isomorphic, as their abelianizations
`ℤ²` and `ℤ³` already show.  Extracting a bijection from two injections is
Cantor–Bernstein, which is unavailable constructively, and the bijection it
yields classically need not be a homomorphism.

For **finite** algebras the repair does work, and that is the setting much of this
library's later work lives in.  Mutual injections between finite carriers force
equal cardinality; an injective map between finite sets of equal cardinality is
surjective; and an injective, surjective homomorphism is an isomorphism, by
`Bijective→≅`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Isomorphisms][].  So on
finite algebras `_≤_`{.AgdaFunction} is antisymmetric up to isomorphism, hence a
partial order on isomorphism classes.  That chain of reasoning is *not* formalized
here; only `Bijective→≅`{.AgdaFunction}, its last step, is.

This module defines the subalgebra relation `_≤_`{.AgdaFunction} and the several
ways of packaging it: as a record bundling both algebras, as a Σ-type over the
smaller algebra with the larger one fixed, and relative to a whole class rather
than to a single algebra.  The class-relative form `_≤c_`{.AgdaFunction} is the
one the closure operator `S`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Varieties.Closure][] is
built from.

<!--
```agda
{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}

module Setoid.Subalgebras.Basic where

open import Agda.Primitive using () renaming ( Set to Type )

-- imports from the Agda Standard Library ---------------------------------------------------
open import Data.Product          using ( _,_ ; Σ-syntax ) renaming ( _×_ to _∧_ )
open import Level                 using ( Level ; _⊔_ )
open import Relation.Unary        using ( Pred ; _∈_ )

-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebra Library ------------------------------------------
open import Overture              using ( proj₁ ; proj₂ ; Signature ; 𝓞 ; 𝓥 )
open import Setoid.Algebras       using ( Algebra ; ov )
open import Setoid.Functions      using ( IsInjective )
open import Setoid.Homomorphisms  using ( hom ; mon ; mon→intohom ; kerquo ; FirstHomTheorem )

private variable α ρᵃ β ρᵇ ℓ : Level
```
-->

The relation comes in two directions and three packagings.

+  `_IsSubalgebraOf_`{.AgdaFunction}, with the infix alias `_≤_`{.AgdaFunction},
   is the relation itself: `𝑨 ≤ 𝑩` is the type of pairs `(h , inj)` with
   `h : hom 𝑨 𝑩` and `inj` a proof that the underlying map of `h` is injective.
+  `_IsSupalgebraOf_`{.AgdaFunction}, aliased `_≥_`{.AgdaFunction}, is the
   converse, and is *definitionally* the same type read the other way round:
   `𝑨 ≤ 𝑩` and `𝑩 ≥ 𝑨` both unfold to an injective homomorphism from `𝑨` into
   `𝑩`.
+  `mon→≤`{.AgdaFunction} turns a monomorphism into a proof of the subalgebra
   relation.  It is immediate, because `mon→intohom`{.AgdaFunction} of
   [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Basic][] already produces exactly this type.
+  `SubalgebraOf`{.AgdaRecord} bundles both algebras and the proof into a single
   record.  `Subalgebra`{.AgdaFunction} instead fixes the larger algebra and
   collects the smaller one with its embedding, so an inhabitant of
   `Subalgebra 𝑨` is a pair `(𝑩 , p)` with `p : 𝑩 ≤ 𝑨`.

```agda
module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥} where
  _≥_   -- alias for supalgebra (aka overalgebra)
    _IsSupalgebraOf_ : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ → Type (𝓞 ⊔ 𝓥 ⊔ α ⊔ ρᵃ ⊔ β ⊔ ρᵇ)
  𝑨 IsSupalgebraOf 𝑩 = Σ[ h ∈ hom 𝑩 𝑨 ] IsInjective (proj₁ h)

  _≤_   -- alias for subalgebra relation
    _IsSubalgebraOf_ : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ → Type (𝓞 ⊔ 𝓥 ⊔ α ⊔ ρᵃ ⊔ β ⊔ ρᵇ)
  𝑨 IsSubalgebraOf 𝑩 = Σ[ h ∈ hom 𝑨 𝑩 ] IsInjective (proj₁ h)

  -- Syntactic sugar for sup/sub-algebra relations.
  𝑨 ≥ 𝑩 = 𝑨 IsSupalgebraOf 𝑩
  𝑨 ≤ 𝑩 = 𝑨 IsSubalgebraOf 𝑩

  mon→≤ : {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ} → mon 𝑨 𝑩 → 𝑨 ≤ 𝑩
  mon→≤ {𝑨 = 𝑨}{𝑩} x = mon→intohom 𝑨 𝑩 x

  record SubalgebraOf : Type (ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} (α ⊔ β ⊔ ρᵃ ⊔ ρᵇ)) where
    field
      algebra : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ
      subalgebra : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ
      issubalgebra : subalgebra ≤ algebra

  Subalgebra : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ → {β ρᵇ : Level} → Type _
  Subalgebra 𝑨 {β}{ρᵇ} = Σ[ 𝑩 ∈ (Algebra β ρᵇ) ] 𝑩 ≤ 𝑨

{- usage note: for 𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ, an inhabitant of `Subalgebra 𝑨` is a pair
   `(𝑩 , p) : Subalgebra 𝑨`  providing
   - `𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ` and
   - `p : 𝑩 ≤ 𝑨`, a proof that 𝑩 is a subalgebra of 𝐴. -}
```

From now on we will use `𝑩 ≤ 𝑨` to express the assertion that `𝑩` is a subalgebra of `𝑨`.

#### Subalgebras of classes of setoid algebras

Suppose `𝒦 : Pred (Algebra α 𝑆) γ` denotes a class of `𝑆`-algebras and `𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ`
denotes an arbitrary `𝑆`-algebra.  Consider the assertion that `𝑩` is a subalgebra of
an algebra in the class `𝒦`.  With the next definition we can express this
assertion as `𝑩 IsSubalgebraOfClass 𝒦`.

```agda
  _≤c_
    _IsSubalgebraOfClass_ : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ → Pred (Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ) ℓ → Type _
  𝑩 IsSubalgebraOfClass 𝒦 = Σ[ 𝑨 ∈ Algebra _ _ ] ((𝑨 ∈ 𝒦) ∧ (𝑩 ≤ 𝑨))
